primaryQuery: Home Assistant Z-Wave JS Server version incompatible
readerQuestion: How do I safely fix the Home Assistant Z-Wave JS Server version incompatible error after an update without resetting or re-pairing my Z-Wave devices?
selectedBecause: Home Assistant 2026.7 raised the required Z-Wave JS server schema, and two separate July community discussions show homeowners reaching the same blocked state through different installation paths. The exact search results expose version requirements and scattered forum fixes, but do not give a current plain-English decision tree for the official app, Z-Wave JS UI, and self-managed server paths. Tara's existing Z-Wave comparison explains which deployment to choose; it does not answer this exact error or the safe recovery order.

demandSignals.evidence: A user upgrading to Home Assistant 2026.7 reported that a remote Z-Wave JS server at version 3.8.0 failed setup because schema 49 was required, and asked how to update a separately installed NPM-based server without losing the working network.

In a separate release discussion, a homeowner said the Home Assistant 2026.7 update left Z-Wave JS UI requiring an update while no update control was visible, prompting a backup restore rather than a clear supported fix.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant 2026.7 release notes
officialSources.supports: Home Assistant 2026.7 requires zwave-js-server 3.9.0 or newer using schema 49, the official Z-Wave JS app 1.4.0 or newer, or the Z-Wave JS UI Docker container 11.19.1 or newer.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant Z-Wave integration documentation
officialSources.supports: The Z-Wave integration connects by WebSocket to a separate server layer; the documentation distinguishes the server, driver, and server URL and documents the official app, Z-Wave JS UI Docker, and self-managed server paths.

officialSources.name: Z-Wave JS UI project documentation
officialSources.supports: Z-Wave JS UI stores persistent files in its store directory and provides the separate server and control-panel path used by container and advanced installations.
